source: Biology - AQA/01 - Cell biology/Questions and Answers/Cell Biology - Questions and Answers.md
sample_definition: Six publicly released June 8461/1H papers, spanning the first assessment and four recent summer series; 2020/2021 emergency autumn series and specimens excluded. No claim of an exhaustive frequency ranking or prediction. Count each type once per paper; overlapping types are allowed.

questions.prompt: Give the main function of the nucleus in an animal cell.
What process takes place in chloroplasts?
Name the tissue at the growing tips of roots and shoots that contains stem cells.
Name the process in which an unspecialised cell becomes a cell with a particular job.
DNA replication happens before mitosis. Give one other change that happens in the cell before it divides.
Describe what diffusion means.
Give one difference between active transport and osmosis, referring to energy.
Before weighing a potato piece after an osmosis investigation, a student gently blots its surface dry. Explain why.
In an antibiotic investigation, one paper disc contains sterile water and no antibiotic. What is the purpose of this disc?
How could a student check whether the results of an antiseptic investigation are repeatable?
A yeast cell is eukaryotic. A bacterial cell is prokaryotic. Give two structures found in yeast cells but not bacterial cells.
Give two advantages of an electron microscope over a light microscope when studying sub-cellular structures.
A light microscope has a ×10 eyepiece lens and a ×40 objective lens. Calculate the total magnification.
Compare what embryonic stem cells and adult bone-marrow stem cells can become.
A drug stops fibres attaching to the copied chromosomes during mitosis. Explain why normal cell division cannot be completed.
A small single-celled organism exchanges enough oxygen through its outer surface. A large multicellular animal cannot do this. Explain why.
A potato cylinder has an initial mass of 3.00 g and a final mass of 2.64 g. Calculate its percentage change in mass.
A student investigates how sugar concentration affects potato mass. Name the independent variable and a suitable dependent variable.
State the function of each structure: cell membrane, mitochondria and ribosomes.
Explain how three features of a sperm cell help it reach and fertilise an egg cell.
The measured length of a cell's image is 36 mm. The cell's real length is 60 µm. Calculate the magnification.
The diagram represents the boundary between a potato cell and the surrounding solution. The membrane lets water pass but prevents the solute shown from crossing.
The concentration of mineral ions is 0.5 arbitrary units in the soil solution and 2.0 arbitrary units inside a root hair cell. Explain how the cell can absorb more of these ions.
Explain how each change increases the rate of diffusion: a higher temperature, a steeper concentration gradient and a larger membrane surface area.
Explain why a student uses a thin layer of onion epidermis, adds iodine solution, and lowers the cover slip at an angle.
Explain why a school bacterial culture is incubated at no more than 25°C, has its lid held with a few pieces of tape, and is stored upside down.
The total circular zone of inhibition around a paper disc has a diameter of 18 mm. Calculate its area, including the disc. Use π = 3.14 and give your answer to 3 significant figures.

A culture starts with 80 bacteria. The population doubles every 20 minutes. Assume nutrients and temperature remain suitable. Calculate the population after 2 hours, giving your answer in standard form.
A grower wants many plants with the same disease resistance as a parent plant. Explain why meristem stem cells are useful.
The diagram tracks two chromosomes in a simplified cell. Each colour represents a different chromosome. Explain how the cell cycle produces two genetically identical daughter cells.
Explain how alveoli are adapted for rapid gas exchange. Link each feature to its effect.
Explain how fish gills absorb enough oxygen from water. Refer to surface area, thickness, blood supply and water flow.
Two cubes have side lengths of 1 cm and 3 cm. Calculate the surface area to volume ratio of each cube. Then explain which cube has the greater surface area relative to its volume.
A student obtains these results after leaving potato pieces in sugar solutions for 40 minutes.
An onion cell image is 5.4 cm long at a magnification of ×600. Calculate the cell's real length in micrometres. State the equation and show each step.
Explain how the small intestine is adapted to absorb digested food efficiently, including absorption by active transport.
A tiny cylindrical structure has a real volume of 6 280 000 nm³ and a real radius of 100 nm. Its image is 2.4 mm long. Calculate the magnification. Use π = 3.14.
Scientists propose using embryonic stem cells to replace damaged nerve cells in a person with paralysis. Evaluate this proposal, including benefits, medical risks and ethical concerns.

review_notes: All questions use new wording or contexts/data and proposed marks; none is presented as a verbatim official question or mark scheme.
Q28 is specification-based bacterial doubling practice; June 2022 Q02.3 supports the transferable time/division calculation, but concerns fungal cells and does not ask exponential bacterial growth.
Q38 extends short-answer stem-cell evidence into an original evaluation task. Q39 and Q42 assemble required-practical methods; their six-mark allocations are original.
The June 2025 mark scheme prints 4.1.3.2 beside Q07.1/Q07.2. Their actual content is stem cells, correctly mapped here to 4.1.2.3.
Current online AQA wording says a maximum of 25 degrees C; the local older PDF says generally 25 degrees C. The current maximum is used.

Excluded clinical drug-testing procedures, immune responses, digestion detail, cancer biology and inheritance mechanisms beyond the Cell biology focus. Application questions supply the necessary context.
This is a focused question bank, not full curriculum coverage. Xylem/phloem and nerve/muscle examples remain available in revision notes.
Six-mark methods and evaluations are read as complete linked answers, not as a universal one-bullet-equals-one-mark rule.
